items.title: Jeff Wilmer, A Better Tent City
notes:
J. Wilmer appeared before Council on behalf of A Better Tent City noting that they have no concerns with the intent of the request for data and reporting in M. Harris’ motion. He explained that they have been in contact with Regional staff to clarify what information would be requested, and don’t have any issues with sharing that information. He stressed that they work with a high needs population and are hoping to use the additional funding to improve the services that they provide.

In response to a question from Council, Peter Sweeney, Commissioner, Community Services, recommended that staff would follow the existing accountability framework for similar organizations, which has been shared with A Better Tent City. Council requested that staff share the criteria as information to Council, and requested a future discussion on the funding criteria.

items.title: Respiratory Season Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner, Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, informed Council that current waste water levels indicate that Covid-19 is decreasing in the community and further noted that both Influenza and RSV rates are currently low. She highlighted that globally there is a significant increase in the rate of Measles but there have been no confirmed cases or contacts in Waterloo Region since 2019. Dr. H. Wang stressed that Measles can cause serious complications and encouraged the public to ensure they are fully vaccinated if travelling.

Dr. H. Wang stated that 18,000 suspension orders were sent out to parents for immunization of pupils. She noted that 10,000 records have been updated since January 1st and encouraged parents to not wait until the deadline. In response to a question from Council, she explained that the letters to parents contain an information sheet in many different languages in an effort to accommodate the many languages spoken within the Region.

motions.item_title: Administration & Finance Committee Summary - February 6, 2024
motions.text: That the following recommendations from the Administration and Finance Committee be approved: 1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the Terms of Reference for the annual Community Capacity Building Fund as set out in report COR CFN 24 002 dated February 6, 2024. 2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2024 allocations under the Key Cultural Institutions grant program as outlined in COR-CFN-24-003 dated February 6, 2024: 1. Approve the 2024 allocation of $840,603 under the Key Cultural Institutions grant program as set out below: a. Kitchener Waterloo Art Gallery - $100,000; b. Canadian Clay and Glass Gallery - $93,587; c. Drayton Entertainment - $261,291; d. THEMUSEUM - $385,725; 2. Fund the additional costs (in excess of the 2024 Budget provision) of $493,450 from the Tax Stabilization Reserve in 2024; 3. Direct staff to include an incremental $493,450 in the Preliminary 2025 Base Budget funded from the property tax levy; and 4.Direct staff to review the KCI program and funding model with the area municipal working group in 2024, and provide an update to Regional Council in Q2 2024 so that there is clarity in advance of 2025 funding requests.
motions.text_html:
That the following recommendations from the Administration and Finance Committee be approved:

1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the Terms of Reference for the annual Community Capacity Building Fund as set out in report COR CFN 24 002 dated February 6, 2024.


2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2024 allocations under the Key Cultural Institutions grant program as outlined in COR-CFN-24-003 dated February 6, 2024:

1. Approve the 2024 allocation of $840,603 under the Key Cultural Institutions grant program as set out below:

a.    Kitchener Waterloo Art Gallery - $100,000;
b.    Canadian Clay and Glass Gallery - $93,587;
c.    Drayton Entertainment - $261,291;
d.    THEMUSEUM - $385,725;

2. Fund the additional costs (in excess of the 2024 Budget provision) of $493,450 from the Tax Stabilization Reserve in 2024;
3. Direct staff to include an incremental $493,450 in the Preliminary 2025 Base Budget funded from the property tax levy; and
4.Direct staff to review the KCI program and funding model with the area municipal working group in 2024, and provide an update to Regional Council in Q2 2024 so that there is clarity in advance of 2025 funding requests.

motions.item_title: Community and Health Services Committee Summary - February 6, 2024
motions.text: That the following recommendation from the Community and Health Services Committee be approved: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to implementing the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) directed growth plan, which prioritizes non-profit growth as outlined in report CSD-CHS-24-001 dated February 6, 2024: Direct staff to explore, where feasible and appropriate, the development of community-based non-profit child care spaces in Regionally owned land/buildings and surplus lands, Waterloo Region Housing redevelopments, and other emerging opportunities. Direct Children’s Services, Housing Services, and Economic Development staff to consult with area municipalities, school boards, universities and colleges, hospitals, other community partners and businesses to explore creating affordable spaces for community-based non-profit child care in under-utilized buildings and lands.
motions.text_html:
That the following recommendation from the Community and Health Services Committee be approved:

  1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to implementing the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) directed growth plan, which prioritizes non-profit growth as outlined in report CSD-CHS-24-001 dated February 6, 2024:
    1. Direct staff to explore, where feasible and appropriate, the development of community-based non-profit child care spaces in Regionally owned land/buildings and surplus lands, Waterloo Region Housing redevelopments, and other emerging opportunities.
    2. Direct Children’s Services, Housing Services, and Economic Development staff to consult with area municipalities, school boards, universities and colleges, hospitals, other community partners and businesses to explore creating affordable spaces for community-based non-profit child care in under-utilized buildings and lands.

motions.item_title: Licensing and Hearings Committee Summary - February 16, 2024
motions.text: That the following recommendation from the Licensing and Hearings Committee be approved: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to taxi fares and the disbursement of accessible taxi funds as outlined in report PDL-CAS-24-001 dated February 16, 2024: Amend the taxi fares in Bylaw 16-044, a Bylaw to Licence, Regulate and Govern Brokers, Owners and Drivers of Taxi Cabs, as follows: Increase the meter drop rate from $3.50 to $4.50; and Approve a new 5-year program to disburse accessibility funds collected by the Region as follows: Increase to Taxi Scrip program funds from $40,000/year to $55,000/year; Increase funds for the Vehicle Conversion Project from $10,000 per vehicle to $40,000 over 5 years to support the purchase of new vehicles; and Increase Fare Subsidy program support from $2.00/trip to $5.00/trip.
motions.text_html:
That the following recommendation from the Licensing and Hearings Committee be approved:

  1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to taxi fares and the disbursement of accessible taxi funds as outlined in report PDL-CAS-24-001 dated February 16, 2024:
    1. Amend the taxi fares in Bylaw 16-044, a Bylaw to Licence, Regulate and Govern Brokers, Owners and Drivers of Taxi Cabs, as follows: Increase the meter drop rate from $3.50 to $4.50; and
    2. Approve a new 5-year program to disburse accessibility funds collected by the Region as follows:
      1. Increase to Taxi Scrip program funds from $40,000/year to $55,000/year; 
      2. Increase funds for the Vehicle Conversion Project from $10,000 per vehicle to $40,000 over 5 years to support the purchase of new vehicles; and
      3. Increase Fare Subsidy program support from $2.00/trip to $5.00/trip.

motions.item_title: Councillor M. Harris Notice of Motion
motions.text: Deferred from February 6, 2024 Community and Health Services Committee Meeting: Whereas, the Region of Waterloo is implementing its Interim Housing Plan while developing a Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, an unprecedented commitment using an all of community approach to ending chronic homelessness in Waterloo Region. Whereas, the 2024 Regional budget included an addition of $10.2 million to address, prevent and end chronic homelessness while the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness will be finalized and delivered in April of 2025, Whereas, an additional $236,390 grant was approved by Council for A Better Tent City, a volunteer-led organization that did not meet the criteria set out in the Region’s Fee-for-Service call for proposals to provide Community Outreach and Support Services, Whereas, agreement outcomes and accountabilities currently exist for similar outreach services funded by the Region of Waterloo, Therefore be it resolved that Regional staff be directed to collect outcomes, data and metrics from A Better Tent City that align with existing homelessness outreach agreements and providers and that such are agreed to with A Better Tent City.
motions.text_html:
Deferred from February 6, 2024 Community and Health Services Committee Meeting:

Whereas, the Region of Waterloo is implementing its Interim Housing Plan while developing a Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, an unprecedented commitment using an all of community approach to ending chronic homelessness in Waterloo Region.

Whereas, the 2024 Regional budget included an addition of $10.2 million to address, prevent and end chronic homelessness while the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness will be finalized and delivered in April of 2025,

Whereas, an additional $236,390 grant was approved by Council for A Better Tent City, a volunteer-led organization that did not meet the criteria set out in the Region’s Fee-for-Service call for proposals to provide Community Outreach and Support Services,

Whereas, agreement outcomes and accountabilities currently exist for similar outreach services funded by the Region of Waterloo,

Therefore be it resolved that Regional staff be directed to collect outcomes, data and metrics from A Better Tent City that align with existing homelessness outreach agreements and providers and that such are agreed to with A Better Tent City.
